signals.detail: Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar disclosed an NVDA buy (traded Oct 23, filed Nov 5); NVDA remains 2026's most congressionally-traded ticker. Separately, Rep. Ro Khanna's family trust sold NVDA on Sept 4 and Oct 7, and Trump also disclosed a sale, shortly before the Jensen Huang 'spy scandal' broke and the stock fell roughly 30% from its highs -- a timing coincidence now drawing political scrutiny, though no evidence of advance knowledge has surfaced. signals.takeaway: NVDA has become a case study in Congress trading on both sides of the same unfolding scandal while retail remains the most engaged counterparty to the stock's volatility.

signals.name: Palantir Technologies
signals.label: Congress consensus + political-risk hire + persistent insider-selling/retail tension
signals.detail: Palantir hired former Sen. Jon Tester as an adviser on Nov 9, explicitly to manage scrutiny of its government contracts now that Democrats have won control of Congress -- a direct response to the bipartisan congressional trading pattern already surrounding the stock. Insider selling remains heavy (reported near $873M over the trailing 12 months with no offsetting insider buys, including a director sale on Nov 2), even as PLTR stays a perennial high-mention WallStreetBets name and the Burry put-position bear case continues to circulate in financial press.
signals.takeaway: Bipartisan congressional interest is now colliding with a company-level defensive hire against the very Congress that's been trading the stock, against a backdrop of one-sided insider selling.

signals.name: Applied Materials
signals.label: Congress + diverging whale 13F bets, now in a steep drawdown
signals.detail: Rep. Josh Gottheimer disclosed an AMAT purchase (traded Oct 26, filed Nov 5) after a September sale. On 13F, Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital opened a $189M position in Q2 while Maverick Capital sold ~99.7% of its stake the same quarter -- and the stock has since fallen sharply from that June 30 reference point. Applied reported earnings Nov 12, with both funds' next 13Fs due by Nov 16, making this an active, unresolved divergence rather than settled consensus.
signals.takeaway: A sitting congressman bought into AMAT at the same time one brand-name hedge fund built a position and another nearly eliminated one -- and the stock's subsequent steep slide means the next 13F round will show who was right.

signals.name: Micron Technology
signals.label: Congress + sharply diverging 13F whales + active retail buzz
signals.detail: 23 members of Congress have disclosed 69 MU trades, including Rep. John McGuire's Oct 1 purchase. On 13F, Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management raised its stake ~1,794% to a $3.63B position in the same quarter David Tepper's Appaloosa cut its MU stake ~41% while still keeping it as a top-5 holding. MU rose sharply on Nov 11 alongside a broader AI-infrastructure rally and was named among the week's most-buzzed retail tickers (alongside AMD, INTC, TSLA, NVDA) in early November.
signals.takeaway: Congressional buying, a dramatic hedge-fund split between a large buyer and a large seller, and heavy retail chatter are all converging on Micron during one of its most volatile stretches of the year.

signals.name: Nebius Group
signals.label: Congress + short-seller vs. retail, now sharpened by a guidance shock
signals.detail: Sen. Alan Armstrong and Trump both disclosed NBIS purchases under the STOCK Act, and Michael Burry disclosed a short position in August as part of a broader AI-infrastructure short basket. NBIS is among WallStreetBets' most-mentioned tickers with a strongly bullish sentiment reading, yet on Nov 12 Nebius beat Q3 revenue estimates but the stock fell ~14% as it guided sharply higher 2027 capex against comparatively modest revenue -- intensifying rather than resolving the AI-spending debate Burry's short represents.
signals.takeaway: Political buyers and a bullish retail crowd are doubling down on Nebius at the exact moment its own guidance handed Michael Burry's AI-spending-skepticism short thesis new ammunition.

signals.name: Benchmark Electronics
signals.label: Congress + institutional 13F convergence, now backed by a real earnings beat
signals.detail: Rep. Gilbert Cisneros and Rep. Josh Gottheimer both disclosed purchases of this ~$2.3B small-cap contract-electronics maker in the same window, alongside a wave of institutional 13F accumulation (Hillsdale, Legal & General, HSBC, First Eagle) that pushed institutional ownership above 92%. The story firmed up further on Oct 28, when Benchmark reported record Q3 revenue (+19% YoY) and raised its full-year 2026 outlook, followed by a Nov 2 announcement expanding U.S. manufacturing for a key customer.
signals.takeaway: Two members of Congress and a cluster of institutional 13F filers converged on an obscure small-cap months before its earnings and contract-expansion news validated the accumulation.

Unlike NVDA/MU, Marvell's Reddit/WallStreetBets mention volume is modest and ranks near the bottom among semiconductor peers tracked, so this is a two-signal-strong, retail-light convergence.
